A student plans to create an alarm system for their room. The room has one door and  
one window.
Three sensors will be used in the system:
 y A sensor to detect movement in the room.
 y A sensor to detect if the door is locked or unlocked.
 y A sensor to detect if the window is open or closed.
The student knows that this practical problem can be expressed in terms of Boolean logic 
and presented in a truth table.
The student considers the following three inputs:
1. MOTION, where true (1), represents that movement is detected in the room and false (0) 
represents no movement is detected.
2. DOOR, where true (1), represents that the door is locked and false (0) represents 
an unlocked door.
3. WINDOW, where true (1), represents that the window is open and false (0) represents 
a closed window.

assessed_concepts: Original source task: Justify the decision of the laptop manufacturer to include both wired and wireless network connection capability.
A portable diagnostic workstation supports both twisted-pair Ethernet and Wi-Fi

markscheme.marking_summary: Ethernet provides a stable connection and avoids radio interference at the desk. Wi-Fi enables movement without trailing cables and connection where wired ports are unavailable. Thus each link supports a different working condition.
source_issues: Source MS universally describes wired bandwidth as much larger than wireless; actual standards vary, so adapted question avoids universal speed assertion.

mappings.scope_evidence:
• Wired transmission via fibre optic cables and twisted pair cables; wireless transmission
• The advantages and disadvantages of these three types of data transmission
• Factors to consider must include bandwidth, complexity of installation, cost, range, susceptibility to interference, attenuation, reliability, security.
